title: Smooth groupoid of unit-framed finite free algebra laws
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and $d\geq1$. For a scheme $T/S$, set $R_T=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and let $FA_d(T)$ be the groupoid of commutative associative $R_T$-bilinear multiplications $m$ on the free module $R_T^d$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] whose unit is the first standard vector $e_1$. An arrow $m\to m'$ is an invertible $R_T$-linear map $g$ fixing $e_1$ with $m'=g^{-1}m(g\otimes g)$; thus $g$ is an algebra isomorphism from $(R_T^d,m')$ to $(R_T^d,m)$. Composition of arrows labelled $g:m\to m'$ and $h:m'\to m''$ is labelled $gh$. Pullback applies the induced map on global sections to coefficients. Define
$$B_d=\mathbf Z[a_{ij}^k\mid1\leq i,j,k\leq d]/\bigl(\sum_l a_{ij}^la_{lk}^q-\sum_l a_{il}^qa_{jk}^l,\ a_{ij}^k-a_{ji}^k,\ a_{i1}^j-\delta_{ij}\bigr),$$
where the denominator denotes the ideal generated by the displayed polynomials (the quotient identifies elements whose difference belongs to this ideal), all indices in each relation range from $1$ to $d$, $\delta_{ij}$ is $1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and polynomial rings are those of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $X=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}B_d$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $b$ be the $d\times d$ matrix whose first column is $e_1$ and whose entry $(i,j)$ for $1\leq i\leq d$, $2\leq j\leq d$ is the variable $b_{ij}$, let $\det b$ be its determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], and put $G=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbf Z[b_{ij}][1/\det b]\bigr)$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the open subscheme of the affine space $\mathbf A^{d(d-1)}_S$ [def-sbc-affine-space] with coordinates $b_{ij}$ on which $\det b$ is invertible; for $d=1$ there are no coordinates, $\det b=1$ and $G=S$. Then matrix multiplication, inverse and identity give $G$ a group structure on its functor of points, with $G(T)$ the invertible matrices over $R_T$ fixing $e_1$. The rule $a(g,m)=g^{-1}m(g\otimes g)$ is a scheme morphism $G\times_SX\to X$. With source $s(g,m)=m$, target $t(g,m)=a(g,m)$, identity $(1,m)$, inverse $(g,m)\mapsto(g^{-1},a(g,m))$, and composition $((h,m'),(g,m))\mapsto(gh,m)$ whenever $m'=a(g,m)$, these maps define a groupoid scheme [def-sfb-algebraic-space-groupoid]. Both $s,t:G\times_SX\to X$ are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For every $T/S$, the coefficient rule $m(e_i,e_j)=\sum_k a_{ij}^ke_k$ identifies its groupoid of $T$-points with $FA_d(T)$, naturally under every base morphism $T'\to T$.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $R$, a bilinear multiplication on $R^d$ is uniquely determined by $m(e_i,e_j)=\sum_k c_{ij}^k e_k$: explicitly $m(x,y)_q=\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}^q x_i y_j$. Comparing the coefficients of $e_q$ in $m(m(e_i,e_j),e_k)$ and $m(e_i,m(e_j,e_k))$ gives precisely the associativity relations defining $B_d$; the symmetry and unit equations give commutativity and $m(e_i,e_1)=e_i$. Bilinearity extends these identities from basis vectors to arbitrary vectors. The polynomial universal property gives evaluation at the $c_{ij}^k$. This evaluation factors uniquely through $B_d$ exactly when the relations vanish: the factor sends a residue class $[p]$ to $p(c)$, well-defined because every element of the generated ideal evaluates to zero. Thus ring maps $B_d\to R$ biject with the required laws.

source.place: Tag 05YP (lemma-represent-FAd), preceding construction of R_univ and m_univ, before equation-objects

proof.text: For every scheme $T/S$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identifies maps $T\to\operatorname{Spec}B_d$ with ring maps $B_d\to R_T$, without any affineness assumption on $T$. By the fibre-product universal property, pairing this map with the given $T\to S$ identifies $X(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,X)$ with the laws from step 1; compatibility over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is automatic because there is just one unital map $\mathbf Z\to R_T$. The identification commutes with $T'\to T$: the map on global sections sends each structure coefficient to its pullback, and therefore sends each defining polynomial relation to the corresponding relation.

proof.text: The polynomial and localization universal properties, the affine-target bijection and the fibre-product universal property identify $G(T)$ with matrices $g$ whose first column is $e_1$ and whose determinant is a unit in $R_T$. These are exactly the invertible matrices fixing $e_1$: a unit determinant gives the inverse $(\det g)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(g)$ by the two adjugate identities; conversely an inverse $h$ gives $\det(g)\det(h)=\det(gh)=1$ by [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities]. All these assertions hold over arbitrary commutative rings. Both the matrix entries and the specified inverse commute with ring maps, since determinants and cofactors are integer polynomials and a ring map preserves the unique inverse of a unit.

source.place: Tag 05YP, construction of G immediately before lemma-represent-FAd; adjugate calculation in algebra.tex Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse), and determinant multiplicativity

proof.text: Put $A=\mathbf A^{d(d-1)}_S$, with its global coordinate matrix $b$ and global section $\Delta=\det b$. The same affine-target and polynomial bijections identify $A(T)$ with all matrices having first column $e_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], $U=D(\Delta)$ is open and $\Delta|_U$ is a unit. A map $f:T\to A$ factors uniquely through $U$ exactly when its image lies in $U$, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. This is exactly when $f^*\Delta$ is a unit: a local homomorphism of local rings reflects units, and inverses of a section whose germs are units exist locally and glue uniquely. Thus $U(T)$ and $G(T)$ are naturally the same subsets of $A(T)$. Yoneda, applied to these mutually inverse natural identifications, gives an isomorphism $G\simeq U$ over $A$. This proves the stated determinant-open description over arbitrary $S$, without assuming $S$ affine.

proof.text: The matrices in step 3 form a group: $(gh)e_1=g(he_1)=e_1$ and $g^{-1}e_1=g^{-1}(ge_1)=e_1$; identity and inverses are the usual ones. Matrix multiplication is associative, as both entries of $(gh)k=g(hk)$ are $\sum_{j,l}g_{ij}h_{jl}k_{lr}$. These operations are natural in $T$, by step 3. The fibre-product universal property identifies points of $G\times_SG$ with pairs of points of $G$, so Yoneda makes multiplication, inverse and identity into scheme morphisms over $S$; it also makes their pointwise group identities equalities of scheme morphisms.

source.place: Tag 05YP, construction of the group functor G before lemma-represent-FAd; categories.tex Tag 001P

proof.text: Given $g\in G(T)$ and a law $m$, define $m'(x,y)=g^{-1}m(gx,gy)$. It is bilinear and symmetric. Also $m'(e_1,x)=g^{-1}m(e_1,gx)=x$ and similarly on the right. Applying $g$ to its two associators gives respectively $m(m(gx,gy),gz)$ and $m(gx,m(gy,gz))$, which agree; invertibility of $g$ proves associativity. Hence $m'$ is a law. Its coefficients are $c'{}_{ij}^q=\sum_{r,u,v}(g^{-1})_{qr}c_{uv}^r g_{ui}g_{vj}$. Step 3 shows that this formula commutes with every map $R_T\to R_{T'}$, so it gives a natural transformation $h_{G\times_SX}\to h_X$. By Yoneda it is a scheme morphism $a:G\times_SX\to X$. This argument proves regularity even though the formula involves $g^{-1}$: that inverse already has entries $(\det g)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(g)$.

source.place: Tag 05YP, displayed formula for a and its omitted verification before lemma-represent-FAd

proof.text: The action identities have the order $a(1,m)=m$ and $a(h,a(g,m))=(gh)^{-1}m((gh)\otimes(gh))=a(gh,m)$: on vectors the middle expression is $h^{-1}g^{-1}m(ghx,ghy)$. In particular $a(g^{-1},a(g,m))=m$. The maps $s,t,e,i,c$ in the statement are scheme morphisms, using the morphisms just constructed, projection, and pairing into fibre products. For a composable pair $((h,m'),(g,m))$ one has $m'=a(g,m)$; its composite $(gh,m)$ has target $a(h,m')$ by the displayed identity. Identity arrows have label $1$, and both composites with the inverse have label $1$. For a triple with labels $g,h,k$ both bracketings have label $ghk$, proving associativity. These are exactly the laws of [def-sfb-algebraic-space-groupoid], with $c(a,b)=a\circ b$; Yoneda turns the verified pointwise laws into scheme identities.

source.place: Tag 05YP, omitted action verification, lemma-represent-FAd, and following paragraph identifying the action groupoid

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], $A\to S$ is smooth for $d(d-1)\geq0$. The open description $G\simeq D(\Delta)\subseteq A$ from step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a),(c) imply $G\to S$ smooth. The projection $s:G\times_SX\to X$ is its base change along $X\to S$, up to swapping the factors, so [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and smoothness under isomorphism imply that $s$ is smooth. The inverse-arrow map $i(g,m)=(g^{-1},a(g,m))$ is an involution by step 7, hence an isomorphism, and $s\circ i=t$. Smoothness under isomorphism, applied to this square over $X$, gives smoothness of $t$. No smoothness of $X\to S$ and no Noetherian, finite-type-base or characteristic assumptions enter.

source.place: Tag 05YP, paragraph after lemma-represent-FAd; morphisms.tex Tags 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), and 01VC (lemma-open-immersion-smooth)

proof.text: Under step 2 the object map is exactly $m(e_i,e_j)=\sum_k a_{ij}^ke_k$. By step 3 a point $(g,m)$ is a permitted invertible linear map fixing $e_1$ together with $m$, and its target is $m'=g^{-1}m(g\otimes g)$. Thus it is exactly an arrow of $FA_d(T)$, including the direction specified in the statement: $g:(R_T^d,m')\to(R_T^d,m)$ is an algebra isomorphism. The two coefficient assignments on objects and arrows are mutual inverses; they preserve identities and the composition label $gh$ by step 7, so give an isomorphism of groupoids. Every assignment commutes with pullback by the explicit coefficient formulas in steps 2, 3 and 6. For $d=1$, the unit relation forces $a_{11}^1=1$, hence $B_1=\mathbf Z$; the matrix is $(1)$ with determinant $1$ and no free entries, so $X=G=S$ and the asserted groupoid is the one-object identity groupoid on every $T/S$.
